ai_positioning.summary: NiSource does not mention artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies in its 10-K filing. The company focuses on traditional utility operations and regulatory compliance.

risks.title: Natural gas commodity price volatility
risks.score_rationale: NiSource's primary operating subsidiaries are natural gas and electric utilities; fluctuations in commodity prices affect operational costs and customer demand patterns, with regulatory recovery mechanisms providing partial protection
risks.summary: The company is exposed to natural gas price volatility and energy demand fluctuations affecting utility operations.

risks.title: Regulatory and environmental compliance
risks.score_rationale: Rate-regulated utility operations are subject to increasing environmental regulations, rate approvals, and decarbonization requirements that impact asset recovery, return on investment, and capital planning
risks.summary: The company must comply with evolving environmental regulations affecting utility operations across six states.

risks.title: Regulatory rate recovery and cost deferral
risks.score_rationale: Critical audit matter shows that rate recovery depends on regulatory commission decisions; failure to recover costs or achieve approved rate of return could materially impact financial results
risks.summary: Regulatory decisions on cost recovery and return on investment are essential to financial performance.

risks.title: Unbilled revenue estimation accuracy
risks.score_rationale: With $465.2 million unbilled revenue recorded, significant variations in customer usage patterns or weather conditions could impact accounting estimates and revenue recognition accuracy
risks.summary: Unbilled revenue estimates based on historical usage, rates, and weather are subject to variance.

risks.title: Weather-dependent customer demand
risks.score_rationale: Utility revenues fluctuate with seasonal temperature variations affecting heating and cooling demand, with particular exposure to heating season volatility
risks.summary: The company's utility operations are affected by weather conditions influencing customer energy demand.

risks.title: Cybersecurity threats to critical infrastructure
risks.score_rationale: As a regulated utility serving six states with critical infrastructure responsibilities, the company faces increasing cybersecurity risks including potential service disruption and data breach threats
risks.summary: The company must protect critical utility infrastructure and customer data against evolving cyber threats.

risks.title: Capital intensity and investment recovery
risks.score_rationale: Regulated utility business model requires continuous capital investment in infrastructure; recovery depends on regulatory approval and rate mechanisms, creating timing and execution risks
risks.summary: The company requires significant ongoing capital investment with recovery dependent on regulatory rate mechanisms.

governance.voting_structure: Majority voting for all directors with resignation policy

company_description: NiSource Inc., an energy holding company, operates as a regulated natural gas and electric utility company in the United States. It operates in two segments, Columbia Operations and NIPSCO Operations. The company provides natural gas to residential, commercial, and industrial customers through approximately 37,300 miles of distribution main pipeline and the associated individual customer service lines; and 310 miles of transmission main pipeline in Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Kentucky, and Maryland. It also generates, transmits, and distributes electricity to approximately 0.5 million customers in various counties in the northern part of Indiana, as well as engages in wholesale electric and transmission transactions. It owns and operates steam coal generating stations in Wheatfield and Michigan City; combined cycle gas turbine in West Terre Haute; natural gas generating units in Wheatfield; hydro generating plants in Carroll County and White County; wind generating units in White County; and solar generating units in Sullivan County, Gibson County, Jasper County, and White County. The company was formerly known as NIPSCO Industries, Inc. and changed its name to NiSource Inc. in A
